titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 105: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 105. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

"11 In ⲛⲟⲩⲣⲏϩ steht ⲩ über der Zeile": the ⲩ stands above the line; the place is named, so it is encoded `\ⲩ/` (48.20, 90.3).

div.p: The manuscript page number ⲣⲉ (top right, odd page) with a bar above and below as the frame (no strokes). Running title > · ⲙⲡⲥⲁϩ · < with its ornaments, no stroke. The text column starts at 530 on this page. Every dot run was counted from the dot x-positions. Every ϣ on the page was checked on a lower-zone sheet at 2.2× and ten of them at 4–8× (3, 8, 11, 14, 20, 23, 29, 33, 35): none is dotted, all have their tail. ⲯ in ⲙⲯⲩⲭⲁⲩⲉ (l. 2) and ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ (l. 24): arms curving upwards and a stem through the baseline, against the straight ϯ of ⲁϯⲧⲉⲓⲃⲉ (l. 9), ϯⲙⲣⲣⲉ (l. 8), ϯⲛⲁϭ (l. 26) and ⲛϥⲣϯϩⲉ (l. 28). Kephalaion 40 (opened 104.21) ends at l. 14 with "leer" and no end sign; kephalaion 41 opens at l. 15. Reconcile flags explained: ll. 16–17 the middle points of the title ornaments (1137, 653); l. 29 the ⲣ dot (813) has area 5; l. 34 the fourteen bracket dots stand at the zone centre (y 1697–1700). Spaces flags are dot runs, enlarged-letter legs (ll. 1, 18, 21, 24, 30, 32), "leer" and the title ornaments and margin numerals.
"leer" after ⲙⲡϫⲁϫⲉ (in the line), then an enlarged Ⲡ (1105–1155) opens a new section in the same line: Ⲡⲙⲁϩϣⲁ|ⲙⲧ (67.3).
Strokes over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ (531–544) and of ⲛⲕⲉⲕⲉ (640–652); diaeresis over ⲓ of ⲡⲥⲁⲓϣ (790–797); dot under the final ⲁ (1241). The bar at 1105–1155 is the top of the enlarged Ⲡ.

Stroke over ⲧ of ⲙⲧ (554–567, 72 %); the bar at 647–655 is the top of ⲃ; measured bar over ⲛⲛ of ⲛⲛⲣⲉϥⲣⲛⲁⲃⲉ (893–912, row 344): first ⲛ (886–901) 53 %, second ⲛ (904–918) 57 % → on both; stroke over ⲣ of ⲣⲉϥⲣ (964–975, 100 %) and a dot under it (969); dot under the final ⲁ (1269). The bar at 1015–1024 is the top of ⲃ.
Stroke over ⲛ of ϩⲛ (628–638); ⲁⲩϣⲱ (ϣ with its tail, 8×); three illegible dots (903, 923, 944); diaeresis over ⲓ of ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ (1269–1277). Bars at 729–738 and 993–1003 are tops of ⲃ.

Stroke over ⲛ of ⲛϩⲃⲏⲩⲉ (701–714); diaeresis over ⲓ of ⲡⲉⲓ (1188–1197); stroke over ⲣ of ⲥⲉⲛⲁⲣⲥⲧⲁⲩ (1278–1289, 100 %); ⲥⲧⲁⲩ|ⲣⲉ runs over the line end (footnote: written in ligature, apparatus). Bars at 737–746 and 1110–1119 are tops of ⲃ.

Stroke over the final ϥ of ⲡⲉⲧⲁϥϫⲉⲥⲧϥ (857–868); diaeresis over ⲓ of ⲁϩⲣⲏⲓ (956–965); measured bar over ⲙⲛ of ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϭ (1088–1107, row 467): ⲙ (1077–1098) 48 %, ⲛ (1100–1114) 57 % → ⲛ only; stroke over the final ⲣ (1273–1284) and a dot under it (1277); ⲥⲉⲛⲁⲣ|ⲥⲗϭⲉ runs over the line end.

A thick bar (530–569, rows 506–508, three rows at grey < 130) stands in the interline between ⲣⲉ of l. 5 and ⲥⲗ of l. 6: 13 px above the x-height of l. 6 and 17 px below the baseline of l. 5. It is straight and of the same thickness as the raised line-end strokes of 103.3 and 105.26, which also stand 10–12 px above their letters; it covers ⲥ (530–541) 100 % and ⲗ (543–560) 100 % (ϭ 21 %) → a supralinear stroke over ⲥⲗ (§4, 105.6). It could also be read as a rule under ⲣⲉ of l. 5 (the footnote on ⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲉ), which the encoding does not adopt (residual risk).

Stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲓⲃⲱⲗⲟⲥ (618–631); strokes over ⲛ of ⲛϩⲁⲉ (774–786), ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲥⲏⲩ (860–873), ⲛ of ⲛϩⲏⲧϥ (1138–1151), its ϥ (1210–1222) and the last ⲛ (1244–1257), with a dot under the last ⲛ (1248). Bars at 573–582 and 667–676 are tops of ϭ and ⲃ.

Measured bar over ⲙⲛ (607–628, row 556): ⲙ (597–617) 50 %, ⲛ (619–634) 60 % → on both (65.29); stroke over ⲛ of ⲛϩⲓⲕⲱⲛ (656–668) and dots under its ⲕ, ⲱ (704, 727); stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲥⲙⲁⲧ (941–954); dot under ⲙ of ⲥⲉⲛⲁⲙ[ⲟⲩⲣ] (1207).

One bar over the first ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ (630–642; the second ⲛ bare) and over the first ⲙ of ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ (696–710); stroke over ⲛ of ϩⲛ (804–817); ϯ of ϯⲙⲣⲣⲉ a straight cross and a stroke over its first ⲣ (877–890, 100 %); strokes over ⲛ of ⲛϩⲁⲏ (937–950) and ⲛⲥⲉ[ⲕⲁ]ⲁⲩ (1185–1198).

The fifth letter of ⲛϩⲩⲡⲟⲡⲟⲇⲓⲟⲛ (606–616) is printed as an open curve with its left side missing (a reversed-ⲥ shape, nothing at x 603–606 even at grey < 170, 8×). The font has no such letter; ⲥ opens to the right. The shape is the ⲟ of this font with its left arc not printed (§3.40) → ⲟ, ⲩⲡⲟⲡⲟⲇⲓⲟⲛ (§4, 105.9). Dots under ⲥ of ϩⲁⲃⲥ (1007) and ⲃ of ⲧⲉⲓⲃⲉ (1116); diaeresis over its ⲓ (1101–1109); ϯ of ⲁϯⲧⲉⲓⲃⲉ a straight cross; five dots inside the bracket (1169–1274). Bars at 986–995 and 1112–1121 are tops of ⲃ.
Strokes over ⲛ of ⲛⲧⲁⲥ (592–604) and ⲛ[ⲟⲩⲱ]ⲛⲉ (1191–1203); dot under the final ⲉ (1297).

Measured bar over ⲙⲛ (633–653, row 722): ⲙ (623–643) 50 %, ⲛ (645–660) 53 % → on both (65.29); stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲥⲛⲉⲩ (1013–1026). ⲛⲟⲩⲣⲏϩ is printed in the line; the footnote places its ⲩ above the line → `ⲛⲟ\ⲩ/ⲣⲏϩ` (48.20). The bar at 756–765 is the top of ϭ.

Dots under both ⲛ of ⲛⲛⲉⲩϩⲣⲁⲩ (575, 592) and a stroke over the first (571–583); measured bar over ϩⲛ of ϩⲛⲁϭⲣⲏⲛ (929–949, row 804): ϩ (921–935) 43 %, ⲛ (940–955) 60 % → ⲛ only. The bar at 984–994 is the top of ϭ.

Dots under ⲁ of ϣⲁ (557), ϩ, ⲉ after the first bracket (666, 681), ⲛ before the second (713) and ⲛ, ⲏ, ϩ, ⲉ after it (786, 804, 821, 836).
Kephalaion number ⲙⲁ (41), centred (820–856), with a bar over both letters.

Title of kephalaion 41, ll. 16–17, each line framed by > · … · <: ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ⲧϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ ⲉⲧⲁⲩⲧⲉϩⲟ ⲡϫⲁϫⲉ ⲉⲧⲃⲉ ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ (ⲉⲧⲁⲩ|ⲧⲉϩⲟ over the line end). The numeral ⲙ̄ⲁ̄ is repeated in both margins with a bar over it (left 573–613, right 1182–1223, glyphs y 958–975, between l. 16 at 946 and l. 17 at 982) → attached to the upper line, l. 16 (30.14, 87.31).
Stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ (905–919). The bar at 728–737 is the top of ⲃ.

Dots under ⲛ before the bracket (718) and ⲩ after it (772); stroke over the final ϥ of ⲁϥⲛ[ⲁ]ⲩϩϥ (806–817).

Stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ (689–703); stroke over ⲛ of ⲙⲛ (944–957; ⲙ bare); dots under ⲡ, ⲟ, ⲗ, ⲉ, ⲙ, ⲟ, ⲥ of ⲙⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ (1102–1200, each matched to its letter's ink column; ⲙ undotted) and under ⲙ, ⲛ of ⲙⲛ (1236, 1255); ϩⲛ bare.

ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ bare (4×); dots under ⲙ, ⲏ of ⲛⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ (1096, 1116). The bar at 975–984 is the top of ⲃ.

Dot under the first ⲁ (536); stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲕⲉⲕⲉ (674–686); dots under ⲃ, ⲱ, ⲕ of ⲡⲉⲧⲁϥⲃⲱⲕ (862, 882, 900); stroke over the first ⲙ of ⲙⲙⲁϥ (1032–1046); stroke over the first ⲣ of ⲁⲩⲣⲣⲣⲟ (1163–1175, 100 %). Bars at 858–867 and 954–963 are tops of ⲃ.
Stroke over ⲙ of ϩⲙ (628–641); stroke over ⲙ of ⲙⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ (789–802); stroke over the first ⲙ of ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ (973–987). The bar at 1108–1116 is the top of ϭ.
